stem: A borrower takes a loan of Rs 50,000 at a flat rate of 12% per annum for 1 year. Under a flat-rate scheme the interest is computed on the original principal for the entire tenure and divided equally across monthly instalments. What is the monthly EMI under this flat-rate scheme?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Total interest = 50000 x 12% = 6000. Total repayable = 56000. Monthly EMI = 56000 / 12 = 4666.67, rounded to Rs 4,667.
Divides only the principal (50000) by 12 and ignores adding the interest portion, giving 50000/12 = 4167, or mistakenly takes round 5000 assuming 12% monthly rather than annual.

Uses interest = 50000 x 10% = 5000 (wrong rate) so total = 55000, monthly = 4583; but here the distractor Rs 4,500 arises from using only 6 months instead of 12 periods: 56000/12.44, a period-count error on a semi-annual misread.
Computes 50000 x 10% = 5000 total interest, giving 55000 / 12 = 4583 due to a rate misread of 10% instead of 12%.

explanation: The flat-rate EMI formula adds total interest (principal x rate x time) to principal and divides by total number of instalments. Here: interest = 50000 x 0.12 x 1 = 6000; total = 56000; EMI = 56000/12 = 4667.

explanation_sections.punchline: Flat-rate interest is computed once on original principal and spread equally; there is no reducing-balance calculation.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the scheme as flat-rate (not reducing balance). Step 1: total interest = P x r x n = 50000 x 0.12 x 1 = 6000. Step 2: total repayable = 56000. Step 3: monthly EMI = 56000 / 12 = 4667.
explanation_sections.lesson: For flat-rate loans, always compute interest on the original principal for the full term before dividing by instalments.
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds. One multiplication and one division. Trap: dividing only the principal by 12 (ignores interest).
